title: 6J Japanese yen · news EMA research
summary: U.S. and domestic news for 6J: five horizons, event types, weekly/monthly breakdowns, EMA sides, distributions and clock-time coverage. Descriptive reconstructed-year evidence with explicit sample sizes.

sections.title: 6J · Japanese yen news calendar
sections.body:
Explore this contract's own U.S. and domestic economic releases. Start with the combined calendar at five following candles, then use the saved-row selectors to change calendar, horizon or news type. Each contract tab has a different eligible release sample; comparisons across tabs are not a common-event ranking.

These are descriptive price-path statistics around a frozen pre-news EMA20/50 direction. Favorable movement, adverse movement and the eventual signed close answer different questions. Positive excursions alone do not establish a tradable edge.

sections.title: Entry, direction and denominators
sections.body:
The entry benchmark is the close of the confirmed 15-minute candle ending at the scheduled release. EMA20 above EMA50 fixes a long side; EMA20 below EMA50 fixes a short side. Equal EMAs skip the signal. The candle opening at the release is the first measured candle; earlier candle ranges do not enter the outcome.

H5/H10/H15/H50/H100 count actual following chart candles. Session gaps and weekends can make elapsed time much longer than candles × 15 minutes. The side never changes within an observation, and later releases do not truncate earlier windows. N means completed outcomes, which alone enter means, quantiles and rates.

MFE is the largest favorable path distance; MAE is the largest adverse path distance. Both are nonnegative distances. Close is signed: positive favors the entry side. MFE / MAE divides average excursions; it is not profit factor. Each normalized outcome is divided by its own entry price before averaging. Ticks refer to this contract's outright quoted price; they are not dollar returns.

sections.title: News types: read the sample size before the average
sections.body:
A timestamp with several selected category types belongs exclusively to Mixed types (same timestamp), code 13. It is not repeated under each component type. U.S.-only and domestic-only selections can classify that timestamp differently, so their type rows must not be added to the combined rows.

Domestic CPI and GDP labels can include different stages or multi-release packages, rather than one uniform announcement series. The tables expose sample size, means, medians, tails and normalized distances so that a large average or a high favorable frequency can be viewed alongside skew and adverse excursions. The n<10 support flag is a descriptive warning threshold, not a statistical significance test.

sections.title: Evidence, reconstruction and native checks
sections.body:
The fixed analysis window starts October 17, 2025 at midnight New York and ends October 17, 2026 at midnight New York, exclusive. The last available price candle is October 16, 2026. The source price year is reconstructed from merged native OHLC with continued EMA seeds; it is not a direct full-year export of the six new indicators.

The source retains native-chart checks covering 621 selected events and 4,968 field comparisons. Those checks concern the native loaded windows, selected entry/type fields and completed five-candle type outcomes; they do not validate every reconstructed-year observation or the other horizons. Abacus retains those receipts and independently checks saved-table aggregation and report transfers; it does not claim a new native TradingView replay.

The new calendar, week, side, hour, year, quarter and distribution summaries group retained per-entry outcomes. They do not rerun price reconstruction or change the saved indicator's entry rule. The earlier report remains separate evidence from its shared U.S. event cohort.

sections.title: Interpretation and practical limits
sections.body:
The expanded contract calendars have different eligible dates and event mixes. They cannot rank currencies on a common experimental cohort. U.S., domestic and combined modes overlap. A U.S. and domestic announcement at one timestamp is one combined observation, while the separate modes can each contain it. Mixed-type rows are exclusive only within their own selected mode.

Calendar archives include corrected historical schedules, not a point-in-time announcement vintage. Release availability and history selection are retrospective. Off-grid releases and unreliable/tentative times are excluded. Overlapping windows, shared macro shocks and repeated horizon views create dependence; small monthly, weekly and news-type groups can be dominated by one event.

No spread, commission, slippage, stop, target, contract sizing or executable entry/exit assumption is tested. Back-adjusted continuous prices and benchmark closes are analytical inputs. Favorable-close frequency is not a trading win rate, MFE/MAE is not profit factor, and normalized price changes are not account returns.

No confidence intervals, multiple-comparison adjustment, causal identification or independent holdout are claimed. The many saved breakdowns are descriptive exploration. Both negative and favorable outcomes belong to the evidence; an apparently strong small cell requires a separately specified follow-up study.
